The objective is to minimize the maximum overlap C₅, measured by the correlation score between the step function and its shifted complement. This approach addresses two main bottlenecks found in fixed-point optimization for high-dimensional nonconvex problems:
- The need for both exploration (global search) to escape local optima and exploitation (gradient-based methods) to refine candidates
- The intractability of the original continuous formulation due to the correlation being a multi-dimensional function
